summary.en-US: Color-code and label Unqork builder components, see which Unqork environment you are on before you act, and inspect or edit page data with built-in debug tools.

description.en-US:
Unqlock makes the Unqork Config builder easier to read. Every one of the 52 component types gets its own color, icon and optional type label, with light and dark palettes and separate controls for icon tints, left accents, full backgrounds and borders. Each effect can be turned on or off for the sidebar and the canvas independently.

A floating badge on Unqork pages names the environment you are looking at, in its own color: STAGING, QA, UAT, PRE-PROD or PRODUCTION, with production marked clearly and anything unrecognized left as UNKNOWN rather than guessed. Visited Unqork hostnames are grouped into organizations automatically, and you can rename groups, correct labels, add your own domains or switch discovery off. Switch links reopen the same path on another host in the same group. Turn on the production guard to disable data edits and component execution on hosts you have marked as production.

Click the badge to open the whole Unqlock menu in the page, or open it from the toolbar button as before. The badge can sit in any corner, show the environment label or just the icon, and be switched off entirely.

Debug tools add three optional actions on Unqork application pages: log submission and cache data to the DevTools console, add, update or remove a top-level submission property, and execute a single component by key. Every mutation and execution asks for confirmation first, production is called out in that confirmation, and nothing runs automatically.

Unqlock makes no external requests and collects no data. Appearance and environment preferences, including saved domain groups, are stored locally in the browser, and discovery records hostnames only, never paths, queries or page data. Debug tools use temporary access to the active tab rather than standing host permissions; opened from the badge, where no toolbar click is available to grant it, they ask for access to that one hostname and keep working elsewhere in the menu if you decline.

version.approval_notes: Unqlock is plain, unminified JavaScript, CSS and HTML with no bundler, minifier or runtime dependency. To reproduce this package: install Node.js 22, then run npm ci followed by npm run build. dist/firefox then contains exactly the files in this submission, and artifacts/unqlock-firefox.zip is the same package. The source archive includes the build scripts, tests and maintainer documentation in .claude/development.md.
